notes.title: Launch Timing, General Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Launch Target: April[/h1]
We are excited to announce that we are officially targeting a launch date in April! The game has not yet been reviewed by Steam staff (which is a requirement for launch), so it is still possible that may change, but we are feeling optimistic about it.

[i]Note: [/i]It has come to our attention that, for some users, the Steam store page has been displaying a launch date of March, 2025. If you were affected by this, please accept our sincere apologies (and a discount on the game). This was an internal target date that was not intended to be displayed on the Steam page. We know firsthand that it sucks when you expect a game to release and it doesn't. If you were affected by this issue, please reach out to us by email or discord and we will happily provide you with a substantial discount code when we launch.

[h1]Expected Launch Functionality[/h1]
We are thrilled with where the game is at, and we are having an absolute [i]blast[/i] play-testing it as we finish up the core feature set for launch.

Currently, here's what we've got for launch:
[list]
[*] You will solve a variety of mysteries ("cases") by interrogating suspects using free-form text.

[*] For each case, you will roleplay as a specific character that you create. You can manage your available characters from the main menu, and you will decide which one to play as when you start a new case.

[*] The suspects you interrogate will be managed by an AI, but they are not just "chat bots"; rather, they are complex agents that simulate a variety of aspects of real people. These suspects are powered by systems that grant them:
[list]
[*] A unique backstory, personality, etc.
[*] Actual simulated emotions that are based on individual emotional profiles and response tendencies
[*] Inherent knowledge or awareness of specific in-game subjects
[*] Certain subjects they will tell the truth about, and certain subjects they will lie about
[*] The ability to reveal more characters for you to interrogate
[*] Custom events that shape their behavior in a variety of ways, such as by influencing their emotions or prompting them to begin telling the truth about something (or covering it up) in response to specific subjects being brought up by the player or certain information being revealed
[/list]

[*] Each suspect will have a variety of "Achievements" that you can get by triggering certain events.

[*] When you think you are ready, you can make a formal accusation:
[list]
[*] If your accusation is correct, you will elicit a confession and the case will be marked as Completed
[*] If your accusation is incorrect, you will be allowed to continue interrogating suspects until you are ready to try again
[/list]

[*] You can work on as many cases as you would like - just start a new save or load an existing one at any time. Each case is standalone, and does not depend on any other cases.

[*] Once you've completed a case, you can:
[list]
[*] Keep talking to suspects to learn more, pursue achievements, or just for fun
[*] Restart the case and try a different approach
[*] Start a new case
[/list]

[*] We currently support the following AI model providers:
[list]
[*] [b]OpenAI:[/b] Cloud solution, makers of ChatGPT.
[*] [b]Anthropic: [/b]Cloud solution, makers of Claude.
[*] [b]Google: [/b]Cloud solution, makers of Gemini.
[*] [b]OLlama: [/b]Local PC solution, which we help you manage in-game.
[*][b] Other/Custom:[/b] Cloud or Local. We support anything that conforms to common OpenAI specifications, and allow you to provide a URL. This should work for a variety of local solutions, such as LlamaSharp, and it should also work for some cloud solutions. (This is actually how we are currently implementing Google Gemini support, under the hood.)[/list]
[/list]
[h1]Built-In Mod Support[/h1]
One of the most exciting aspects of the game is that it will offer [b]full modding support[/b] on day one. We intend to only ever develop game content for AI Interrogation Simulator using features that our modding community can also use. That means the community will have every bit of the power at their fingertips when making content that we do, and when we release new gameplay features we will always give them to the modding community at the same time.

Mods can be used to:
[list]
[*] Create new cases to be solved
[*] Override content in the cases that come with the base game
[*] Interact with all mechanical aspects of NPC creation
[*] Provide character templates for players to use when starting cases
[/list]

[h1]Community Involvement[/h1]
We have big plans for community involvement! AI Interrogation Simulator is already a great experience, but we think there are plenty of opportunities for enhancement. We think it's important that the community have a real say in how things turn out, and we will be collecting feedback throughout the Early Access period and beyond.

It is our commitment to you, our players, that we will only release games and content to you when we sincerely feel they are ready for prime time. That means we will do our very best to ensure that Early Access is always a collaboration opportunity, and never an unpaid beta test.

If you have a feature you'd like to see, a new cloud model you want supported, or anything else - you can reach out to us on our Discord server and we will be happy to take your feedback.

[h2]Modding Community[/h2]
If you are a content creator who is already excited to get involved, feel free to reach out! We are very excited to support the community however we can, and we are open to licensed content deals if you would like your mod content included in the base game.

[b]A quick promise: [/b]We will only ever include your content in the base game with your permission, and we will compensate you with a percentage of our profits if we do so. We are not interested in taking unfair advantage of our modding community, nor do we see them as an extension of our content production wing. A sincere and respectful relationship between developers and modders is the bedrock of the modern gaming ecosystem, and it is important to us that we honor that.

[h1]FAQ[/h1]
[h2]Why do I have to connect to a separate AI?[/h2]
This is something we put a lot of thought into. Originally, we planned to seamlessly support local model integration by shipping a small AI model with the base game. However, AI models are not a one-size-fits-all solution, and decent models generally weigh in at several gigabytes or larger.

We decided that it made the most sense to simply provide players with a variety of options, ranging from major providers like OpenAI to self-hosted local models. We want to let [b]you[/b] make the final decisions about which models are used in-game. And, instead of bundling a hefty local model into the game that may or may not be right for you, we included a guided OLlama integration that will help you pick a local model out and get it set up.

[h3]Why doesn't the game just ship with a built-in local AI model as a default?[/h3]
As mentioned above, the main challenges with local models are:
[list]
[*] Good models have large file sizes.
[*] The best model for you depends on your hardware.
[/list]
As such, we didn't want to use up our players' valuable disk space and network bandwidth just to install a local model that may not be right for them.

[h3]Couldn't you have provided a SaaS solution with some tokens included in the purchase, though?[/h3]
Yup - we could have, and it would have been the most convenient option. That's why a number of AI-powered games on the market have taken that approach.

There's a major problem with providing our own SaaS solution and giving you tokens for it that we just couldn't get past, though: [b]it would ultimately be more expensive for you, the player[/b].

Frankly, we suspect that bundling our own SaaS solution may have even been the most profitable move for us; maybe that's why so many companies are doing it. But, it would have come at the cost of game quality, and that's a sacrifice we simply were not willing to make. If you want a managed service, connecting to a cloud provider like OpenAI should only take a few minutes - and by doing so, you will be in total control of your experience.

We are making the bet that our players will be willing to take this extra step. If the community resoundingly requests that we release our own managed service, we will consider doing so. However, at this time, we genuinely do not believe it is the right direction for our game or for the video games industry as a whole.

[h1]Who We Are[/h1]
We are a team of long-time gamers who are sincerely thrilled to be building this awesome game, and we've got a lot of big plans! This is a "by gamers, for gamers" situation. That is to say, we are only interested in making games that we are also excited to play, because we think that's an important part of creating great work. Likewise, we know what it's like to be on the player-side and it's important to us to make it a great experience.

Our primary goal as a studio is to bring you the best AI-powered video games on the market. We believe the existing technologies are grossly underutilized...and we look forward to proving it.

We also aim to combat the steady rise of AI-powered video games that are designed to suck as much money or data out of players as possible. You aren't a number, to us; you're a person. We aren't going to sell your data, we aren't going to spy on your conversations with the AI, and we aren't interested in compromising the quality of our games just so we can sell you some tokens.

[i]We'd like to go ahead and say the quiet part out loud:[/i] We think it's pretty gross that so many AI games today require you to buy their in-house tokens to play their game, or demand a monthly subscription, when they could just give you direct access to the third-party providers (like OpenAI) that they're often already using under the hood.

[b]The game is the product - not you![/b] We just hope you will buy a copy, have as much fun as we are, tell your friends about it, and hopefully get hyped to buy whatever cool stuff we make next. Call us old fashioned?

[h1]Where to Find Us[/h1]
Email Address: contact@arbonix.ai
Discord Link: https://discord.gg/mwyQxsMc2u

[h1]Thank you![/h1]
We are so, so excited to put this game in your hands. We truly believe it will be the best AI-powered game experience on the market. We'll keep you posted!
[i]- Team Arbonix[/i]
